Day 16 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

Auto Scaling

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic verified by artifact

Auto Scaling Groups maintain a desired fleet and can change capacity in response to health and demand instead of treating one server as permanent.

Architecture / mental model

Launch Template → Auto Scaling Group → instances across subnets → health / scaling signals

How it works

An Auto Scaling Group defines minimum, desired and maximum capacity and launches instances from a launch template. The group continuously tries to keep actual capacity aligned with desired state.

Scaling policies can adjust capacity from metrics or schedules, while health checks can trigger replacement. The design becomes stronger when instances bootstrap themselves instead of depending on manual configuration.

Scaling the application tier does not automatically scale databases, queues or other shared dependencies. Capacity planning still follows the whole request path.

Hands-on reference

aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups
aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities

Verification

Inspect desired versus in-service capacity, recent scaling activities and health status. In a lab, terminate one managed instance and observe whether the group restores desired capacity.

Field note / gotcha

Auto Scaling can faithfully create more broken instances if the launch template or bootstrap process is broken. Replacement is not repair.

Security considerations

Keep instance roles least-privileged, protect launch-template user data and ensure replacement instances receive security configuration consistently.

What I learned

Elasticity depends on disposability. A server that requires manual rescue every time it is replaced is not really part of an automated fleet.
